title: autotune: default batching/caching profiles, quantization presets, and unit-econ tooling
author: Jordan Kim
description:
Motivation: Out-of-the-box defaults for batching and KV-caching plus curated quantization profiles significantly reduce per-token costs for common workloads. This PR centralizes autotune defaults and adds a unit-economics toolkit to estimate expected cost/latency trade-offs for a given traffic mix and model selection.

What this PR does: consolidated default batching/caching profiles into runtime/config/autotune_defaults.yaml; introduced quantization presets for xformers/pytorch runtime (q8_0/q4_0/q4_1) and a mapping from workload types to recommended presets; implemented a unit-econ CLI + small web UI export (tools/uecon) that ingests route-level metrics and outputs recommended profile configs and estimated monthly savings; wiring to the optimizer service so RecommendedProfiles can be surfaced in Console.

Why: Customers repeatedly ask for safe defaults that reduce cost without manual tuning. This aims to give teams a low-friction first improvement and a data-driven path to further tuning.

Scope and trade-offs: defaults are conservative and guarded by safety checks (max_latency_slo increase guardrails). Quant presets are documented and include fallback rules for correctness regressions. The unit-econ tool uses sampled metrics and a simple Monte Carlo estimator (configurable) — it is intended for planning/ops, not billing accuracy.

Checklist: 
- [x] Consolidate defaults and add migration path
- [x] Add quant presets and runtime feature flags
- [x] Add unit-econ tooling + tests and E2E with sample dataset
- [x] Add Console UI hook and recommended-profile API field
- [x] CI green and perf canary ran on staging

Testing: unit tests for autotune defaults and quant mapping, integration tests for optimizer-uecon API, staging canary with 3 customer-like workloads (chat/short generation/embeddings) showing ~18-32% cost reduction on average with <5% latency regressions when using conservative presets.

Notes: Migration: runtime will prefer explicit per-route settings, then account-level recommended profile, then autotune defaults. There is a rollout flag (autotune_defaults_v1) to enable gradually. See RELEASE_NOTES in repo root for migration steps.

file_snippets:
runtime/config/autotune_defaults.yaml: |
  # conservative batch and cache defaults for common workloads
  default: 
    batching: 
      max_batch_size: 64
      max_wait_ms: 8
    kv_cache: 
      prefix_cache_enabled: true
      max_prefix_tokens: 256

canary_summary: Staging canary executed across 3 workload profiles (chat, short-gen, embeddings). Results: conservative presets -> 18% avg cost reduction, 0.8% p50 latency improvement, 3.2% p95 regression (within guardrails). Aggressive presets -> up to 32% cost reduction but observed 7-12% p95 regressions on some long-context chat traces; aggressive presets remain behind feature flag.
release_notes: Add autotune defaults for batching and KV caching; introduce curated quantization presets (q8_0, q4_0, q4_1) with safe fallbacks; add unit-econ tooling and Console recommendations API. Default rollout is conservative; aggressive quant presets are behind opt-in feature flag.
notes_for_ops: To roll out: enable autotune_defaults_v1 feature flag at account-level, run tools/uecon/cli estimate --dataset <route_metrics> to generate recommended profiles, validate in staging canary, then enable per-route. For aggressive quant presets, ensure model-level accuracy tests are available before enabling.
estimated_savings_summary: Based on staging traffic profile, expected savings: chat-heavy apps: ~22% monthly token cost reduction, embeddings-heavy: ~18% reduction, mixed workloads: 15-28% depending on quant aggressiveness and cache hit rate.
hotfix_followups: Issue: observed rare correctness regression on model family X-2 when q4_1 used; follow-up created ENG-4737 to add per-model canary checks.
